forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

compliance.notes: Re-scored with the standalone Capital Strategy 2026 read alongside the TMSS. Strongest areas: the Annual Investment Strategy (SLY-driven creditworthiness with CDS/market-data overlays and comprehensive counterparty/group/country/sovereign limits), the MRP policy (methods, asset-life basis and GBP3.998m overpayment disclosed), the CFR/capital-expenditure reconciliation, the scheme of delegation, and - now the capital strategy has been read - a genuinely long-term capital strategy (30-year Strategic Capital Requirement and quantified revenue impact). Weakest areas remain the liability benchmark (entirely absent though the GBP21.7m CFR is 100% internally borrowed and GBP50m of HDL borrowing is planned) and commercial proportionality (COM-03: the proportionate-investment objective is stated and the exposure and reserves are disclosed, but no exposure-vs-reserves headroom test is performed - the GBP50m HDL facility exceeds total reserves). Reading the capital strategy IMPROVED four requirements: CS-01 (2->3), CS-02 (2->3), CS-05 (2->3) and PI-08 (0->1), and firmed the evidence for CS-03, COM-01/02/03/04/06/07/09, GOV-06, KS-03 and RISK-05. Other gaps: no sterling-only borrowing statement (BOR-03), no derivatives policy (RISK-06), PI-08 income-dependence ratio still not presented as an indicator. Not applicable: CS-06 (treasury not delegated), COM-11 (holds material non-treasury investments), MRP-04 (England).

gaps.evidence: Cap Strat p.14 sec 9.4-9.6 commercial/service income streams supporting the general fund (EFS rent GBP1.7m 2026/27; HDL loan interest; HLL loan interest); TMSS p.18 Tables 10/11 forecast income Capital Loans GBP324k + Working Capital Loans GBP581k
TMSS p.16 Table 8 investment fixed/variable rate exposure limits (100%/75%)

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Shared Internal Audit Service Report - Community Infrastructure Levy 2025-6
findings.headline: The Council has not carried out Subsidy Control Act assessments on its commercial CIL awards
findings.detail: The report says that Subsidy Control advice was not sought before the Potters Bar Football Club award, and that legal advice is now being sought for the Borehamwood Football Club bid. It recommends a structured assessment against Principles A to G for every commercial bid.
findings.matters: A subsidy control risk on public money given to private companies is a legal exposure that would affect any council funding similar private projects.
findings.quote: No such assessment has been undertaken when the Council has engaged, or are considering engaging, with commercial organisations.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Shared Internal Audit Service Report - Community Infrastructure Levy 2025-6
findings.headline: The Planning Service had 20 days to analyse the bids in the February 2026 CILIP cycle, which the audit says covered nine bids totalling circa £13.8m
findings.detail: The report states the bid deadline was 6 January 2026 and the CILIP papers deadline was 3 February 2026. It also records emergency CILIP meetings held to speed funding, including one £2,000,000 bid that had under two days for due diligence.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would recognise the capacity gap between bid volume and officer time to assess large grant requests.
findings.figures: 20 days; nine bids; circa £13.8m; £2,000,000 bid with less than two days for due diligence
findings.quote: With the bid deadline being 6 January 2026, the Planning Service had just 20 days to analyse and make recommendations on spend

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Shared Internal Audit Service Report - Community Infrastructure Levy 2025-6
findings.headline: A £1.865m bid scored 37 out of 145 points in officer quality assessment, and the audit recommended deferring it
findings.detail: The audit states the bid had one quote, one school reference, and a 503-word application across 19 questions. The report recommended deferring the bid to the March 2026 CILIP meeting until the vetting was complete.
findings.matters: A bid below any quality threshold reaching a member decision is the scoring control gap other councils would want to rule out in their own processes.
findings.figures: £1.865m bid; 37 out of 145 quality points; 503 words; 19 questions
findings.quote: A £1.865m bid, scoring only 37 out of 145 points in quality assessment

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Shared Internal Audit Service Report - Community Infrastructure Levy 2025-6
findings.headline: The Council has not published an Infrastructure Funding Statement since the 2023/24 monitoring period, and management has set a target of December 2026 to publish the 2024/25 and 2025/26 statements
findings.detail: The audit says the 2023/24 statement did not contain an evidenced Infrastructure List of what CIL could be spent on. Legislation requires the statement to be published every year by 31 December.
findings.matters: A council without a current IFS cannot show the CIL spend or pipeline that the legislation requires it to publish, which is a transparency gap other councils would check against their own statements.
findings.figures: Target Date: 24/25 and 25/26 IFS to be published by end December 2026
findings.quote: The Council have not published a current Infrastructure Funding Statement on their website, with the most recent report for the 2023/24 monitoring period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Shared Internal Audit Service Report - Community Infrastructure Levy 2025-6
findings.headline: All CIL and NCIL bids agreed from April 2026 are subject to Legal Agreements, according to the management update
findings.detail: The audit's recommendation was that funding and community use agreements should be signed before payments are authorised. Management's update says the new rule applies to all CIL and NCIL bids agreed from April 2026 onwards.
findings.matters: A rule requiring signed agreements before payment is a control that other councils can benchmark against their own grant-payment practices.
findings.quote: All bids agreed from April 2026 onwards (CIL and NCIL) all subject to Legal Agreements.
